newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INTERVIEW-HK's Tsang welcomes China backing dollar.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-HK's Tsang welcomes China backing dollar.

text.p: China's help in defending the Hong Kong dollar in cases of stress would be helpful but such a scenario is unlikely, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Tuesday.

China and Hong Kong are among the Asian countries that have signed a pact on repurchasing U.S. dollar government securities from each other as a way of maintaining liqudity and currency stability in times of difficulty.

"China is a partner in this so in any case of stress with the Hong Kong dollar, any offer of help will be helpful, no matter how remote the circumstances might be," Tsang told Reuters Financial Television in an interview on Tuesday.
"I would regard a raid on the Hong Kong dollar as a very rare event," he said.
Hong Kong's participation in the repo pacts was designed to further strengthen the fundamnetals of the Hong Kong dollar.
Tsang said that Hong Kong has healthy foreign currency reserves of US$62 billion and that the currency is trading on the strong side of its pegged range against the U.S. dollar.
The territory practices prudent fiscal policy and is running a budget surplus, he said.

China also has said it would support Hong Kong's securities markets, but central bank governor Dai Xianglong last week denied that China was putting together a 300 billion yuan bail out fund in case of instability.
Tsang said he believed the securities market should be allowed to run its "own voluntary course unless intervention is quite necessary."

Asked if market sentiment would be helped or hurt by China's aid in financial markets, Tsang said "the intention of help on the currency side is helpful and stabilising, but going beyond that, it becomes more debateable and more controversial."
